title: Regulating Professional Players in Peer-to-Peer Markets: Evidence from Airbnb
authors: Wei Chen; Zaiyan Wei; Karen Xie
near_miss_reason: Staggered city-level regulation of professional Airbnb hosts (zip-code x month panel, 10 cities, Oct 2014-Jul 2017; adoption Apr 2016 in San Francisco and New York, Feb 2017 in Portland, plus one NYC zip each in May and Aug 2016), estimated by areg with zip-code FE and year-month FE. Every main-text column (Tables 4-10) also includes eight time-varying ACS zip-code controls AND ten city-specific linear time trends (boston_trend ... wash_trend), i.e. assignment-unit-specific trends; Tables 8-10 additionally add policy x price-dispersion (subgroup-by-treatment intensity interaction).
near_miss_5c_note: Not 5c-eligible: city-specific linear trends (assignment-unit trends, Hull's unit-trend rule) appear in every column alongside the ACS controls. Moot in any case: the Airbnb outcomes are not shipped.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: From policy_dummy in the shipped paper_data_shared.dta: first-treated month 675 (2016-04; 26 SF + 151 NYC zips), 676 (1 NYC zip), 679 (1 NYC zip), 685 (2017-02; 32 Portland zips). 7 never-treated cities (212 zips).
eligible_reason: Design is staggered (city-level professional-host regulations at three cities with different start months, seven never-treated cities) with zip-code and year-month FE, but every reported column adds time-varying ACS zip-code controls and city-specific linear trends (outreg rows 'City time trends: Yes'), which violate the controls and unit-trend rules; Tables 8-10 add policy x dispersion interactions. No qualifying column. Airbnb outcome data (AirDNA) are under NDA and not shipped.
design_notes: Stata areg y policy_dummy ACS_controls city_trends i.reportingmonth1, absorb(zipcode) vce(cluster zipcode). Outcomes: log number of professional/nonprofessional/total properties and hosts (Tables 4-5), log median nightly rates (Table 6), top/bottom nonprofessional prices and reservation days (Table 7), moderation by price dispersion (Tables 8-9), total reservation days and revenue (Table 10). Tables 2-3 (R) are descriptive/PSM comparisons of property characteristics before the policy announcement. Matched zip codes per the README ('final matched zip codes').

specs.exclusion_reason: time-varying ACS controls (8) and city-specific linear trends (10) in every column
specs.outcome: log_pro_prpty, log_pro_host, log_nonpro_prpty, log_nonpro_host, log_ttl_prpty, log_ttl_host, log_nonpro_price, log_pro_price, log_all_price, log_nonpro_price_top/bottom, log_nonpro_rsrvday_top/bottom, log_ttl_rsrvday, log_ttl_revenue

specs.exclusion_reason: policy x price-dispersion interaction (subgroup-by-treatment intensity) plus controls and city trends

data_files_note: paper_data_shared.dta ships only the zip-code x month frame, ACS controls, city trends, city and policy_dummy (14,163 rows, 422 zips, 34 months); the AirDNA outcomes (airbnbreg_data.dta) are under NDA and must be purchased from AirDNA.
data_provenance_note: Outcome variables not shipped (AirDNA NDA); only controls and treatment timing are included.
software_notes: Stata 14-16 (areg, outreg); R for Tables 2-3; Python notebook for Figure 1
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text or PDF). Adoption timing verified in paper_data_shared.dta. Near-miss on design (controls + city trends), not 5c-eligible, and outcome data not shipped.
